1	You are adjudicating disagreements between a benchmark case's answer key and an independent expert's blind solution. For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.
2	
3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to a substantive (not merely evidence-gathering) intervention? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.
9	
10	Truth convention: expected answers are what a careful analyst concludes after reading the initial file plus the optimal read path (at most three catalogue items); for INCOMPLETE and NOCONC cases, what the whole catalogue supports.
11	
12	FLAGGED ITEMS: IT-R3: 'unknown' is also defensible. Overtime hours themselves rose only modestly, since call-back pay is mostly the 3-hour minimum on short rounds, and no claimant-level hours data exist (C4)., IT-A4: 'harmful' is also defensible, because a written reprimand without evidence of favoritism risks punishing the wrong party.
13

15	IT-R3: 'unknown' is also defensible. Overtime hours themselves rose only modestly, since call-back pay is mostly the 3-hour minimum on short rounds, and no claimant-level hours data exist (C4).: (no answer)

310	CASE OD2-DEV-OBVWRONG (OBVWRONG, organizational): Larkmoor Parks: the maintenance overtime overrun
311	Setting: The Larkmoor Parks and Open Space Department (fictional) maintains parks in four districts: Riverside, Eastgate, Millbrook and Summit Hill. The maintenance division has 112 maintenance-worker positions. This year the city adopted several budget reductions, including a citywide hiring freeze from 6 January. Maintenance overtime for April–September is well over budget, and the council's Finance Committee wants an explanation and a corrective plan.
312	Presenting request: The Budget Office has asked you to explain the overtime overrun in the parks maintenance division and recommend what the department should do before the Finance Committee deadline of 15 December. The Director believes the hiring freeze is the cause and has asked for an exemption to fill eleven positions.
313	INITIAL EVIDENCE
314	E1 [stage S1] Office of Budget & Management memo to the Parks Director (financial-record): Re: Overtime variance, April–September. Parks maintenance overtime for April–September totals $688,400, compared with $412,100 for the same months last year (+67%) and a budget of $430,000. Council's Finance Committee has asked for an explanation and corrective plan by 15 December. For reference, this year's adopted reductions for the department were: citywide hiring freeze on non-public-safety positions (from 6 January); deferral of two mower replacements ($118,000); non-renewal of the after-hours closing services contract ($96,000); reduced seasonal temp hours ($40,000). Please route your response through this office.
315	E2 [stage S1] Interview notes, Director Ruth Okafor-Lind, 3 November (leadership-account): 'This is the hiring freeze, plain and simple. We started the year six maintenance workers short and we're at seventeen now. Every vacancy is a route somebody has to cover after their shift. July was brutal too, because the heat meant extra irrigation checks and mowing catch-up. I've asked the City Manager for an exemption to fill eleven positions; that brings overtime back to normal within a quarter.' Asked about other drivers, she said the closing contract 'was a small line, crews absorbed it.' She said she had not seen a breakdown of overtime by pay code.
316	E3 [stage S1] HR/payroll extract prepared at the Director's request (system-record): Maintenance division, current year. Month: vacant maintenance-worker positions (of 112) / overtime paid. Jan 6 / $52.3k; Feb 8 / $49.1k; Mar 10 / $55.0k; Apr 12 / $104.2k; May 15 / $109.0k; Jun 17 / $118.1k; Jul 17 / $121.4k; Aug 17 / $119.3k; Sep 17 / $116.4k. HR analyst note: correlation between monthly vacancies and monthly overtime, January–September, r = 0.93. 'Overtime has tracked the vacancy count closely all year.'
317	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Dale Visconti, crew lead, Millbrook district, 5 November (staff-account): 'We're running routes two and three people short. Guys are holding over an hour or two most days to finish mowing. On top of that, since spring we're back out at night a few times a week, and nobody's seen their kids in months. Morale is the lowest I've seen in nineteen years. If they'd just fill the positions this would sort itself out.' He estimated he personally had worked 'about 25 hours of overtime a month' since April.
318	E5 [stage S1] City Ethics Hotline intake record #2611 (log): Received 22 August from an anonymous caller identifying as a parks employee. Allegation: two Riverside maintenance workers (named in the sealed record as Employees R-14 and R-22) 'are claiming night call-backs for parks they never go to. It's all paper slips, nobody checks. They're each pulling an extra grand a month.' Caller declined follow-up contact. Status: referred to Internal Audit for review on 26 August.
319	E6 [stage S1] Email from the Municipal Employees Local 418 steward to the Director, 7 November (staff-account): Members are exhausted and grievances are coming. Two points. First, in Eastgate the night lock-ups keep going to the same handful of people the supervisor likes, and others never get asked. Second, if management answers this with an overtime cap, understand that members will stop taking call-backs, and then the gates and restrooms don't get locked. Nobody wants a repeat of the splash-pad break-in two years ago. Fill the vacancies and treat people fairly.
320	E7 [stage S1] Risk Management quarterly summary, parks maintenance (system-record): Workers' compensation claims filed April–September: 15 (prior year, same period: 9). Claim types: strains/sprains 8, lacerations 3, slips/falls 3, other 1. Lost workdays: 112 (prior: 61). Safety coordinator's note: 'The rise coincides with heavy overtime; fatigue is a likely factor and we recommend a review.' No analysis of hours worked by individual claimants has been performed.
321	CATALOGUE (full contents)
322	C1 [stage S1] City Manager hiring-freeze directive and citywide exemption log - City Manager's Office (document): Directive 2026-01 freezes all non-public-safety hiring from 6 January until further notice. Departments may request exemptions for positions 'essential to health, safety, or legally mandated service.' Exemption log to date: 9 requests citywide, 4 approved (all in the water utility and 911 dispatch). Parks submitted one request on 28 October for 11 maintenance-worker positions; it is pending. The directive does not restrict overtime or contract spending.
323	C2 [stage S1] Regional weather station summary, April–September, current and prior year - Larkmoor airport weather station (external-data): Days at or above 35°C: 6 (prior year 2). Mean July high 31.8°C (prior 30.1°C). April–September rainfall 388 mm (prior 402 mm). Growing-season degree days +4%. All four parks districts lie within 9 km of the station; no district-level variation is recorded.
324	C3 [stage S1] Budget office overtime workbook by pay code and district, April–September, current and prior year - Office of Budget & Management, payroll analytics (financial-record): April–September, prior year → current year. By pay code: OT-X holdover $341.0k → $358.1k (hours +1.5%; rest reflects the 3.5% July wage increase); CB call-back $38.2k → $289.3k; other (holiday, storm, event) $32.9k → $41.0k. By district: total OT, call-back portion, and vacant positions at 30 September. Riverside $112k → $205k, CB $10k → $95k, 5 of 30 vacant. Eastgate $104k → $200k, CB $9k → $98k, 1 of 30 vacant. Millbrook $98k → $179k, CB $9k → $84k, 6 of 28 vacant. Summit Hill $98k → $104k, CB $10k → $12k, 5 of 24 vacant. Call-back entries: 2,295 (prior 312); 1,962 carry task code CLOSE (prior 0), all dated 1 April or later, none in Summit Hill; other call-backs 333. Data aggregated by district; no employee-level detail.
325	C4 [stage S1] Workers' compensation claim log, parks maintenance, April–September - Risk Management claims system (system-record): Fifteen claims. Each entry lists date, time of injury, task and injury type; the district field is blank on most entries. 11 of 15 injuries occurred between 07:00 and 13:00; 9 involved mowing, trimming or lifting. The claim form does not record hours worked in the preceding 24 hours or whether the employee had worked a call-back the previous night, and payroll records have not been matched to claims. The prior-year log shows a similar task mix (6 of 9 involved mowing, trimming or lifting).
326	C5 [stage S1] Collective agreement excerpts, Articles 12 and 14 (overtime and call-back) - City–Local 418 collective agreement (document): Art. 12.3: work beyond the scheduled 8-hour shift is paid at 1.5× in 15-minute increments. Art. 12.7: management may not change regular shift start times without 30 days' notice and consultation. Art. 14.1: an employee recalled to work after leaving the worksite receives a minimum of three hours' pay at 1.5×, regardless of time worked. Art. 14.4: call-back is voluntary unless no volunteer is available, in which case the least-senior qualified employee is directed. Wage schedule: 3.5% increase effective 1 July.
327	C6 [stage S1] Procurement file for the after-hours closing services contract, with related operational memo - Purchasing Division file PK-2219; Deputy Director memo of 24 March (change-record): Contract PK-2219 with Kestrel Night Services covered nightly closing of gates, restrooms and splash pads at 41 sites in Riverside, Eastgate and Millbrook for $96,000 a year. It expired 31 March and was not renewed (adopted budget reduction). Summit Hill's 12 sites are closed under a separate contract paid by the Summit Hill Business Improvement District, which continued unchanged. Memo, Deputy Director Paul Senanayake, 24 March: 'From 1 April, nightly closing at the 41 sites will be done by maintenance staff on call-back under Art. 14. Supervisors will post sign-up sheets. Closing is a condition of the city's liability coverage and must not be skipped.' Margin note: 'Net saving est. $60k after modest OT.'
328	C7 [stage S1] HR exit interview summaries, maintenance workers separating January–September - Human Resources (document): Eleven separations (8 resignations, 3 retirements). Primary reasons cited by those who resigned: higher pay elsewhere (5), commute or relocation (2), conflict with a supervisor (1). Three mentioned 'too much overtime' as a secondary reason. Under the hiring freeze, no position was backfilled.
329	C8 [stage S1] Interview with the Eastgate district supervisor - Interview notes, Marisol Adeyemi-Clark, Eastgate supervisor, 10 November (manager-account): 'I post a sign-up sheet every Monday for the week's closings. The same five or six people sign up most nights, because others have childcare or second jobs. If nobody signs, I direct the junior person, like the contract says. I don't keep the old sheets; they go in the bin when the week's over.' She said no one had told her about a complaint. She declined to estimate how call-backs were split among her 29 staff.
330	C9 [stage S1] Internal Audit memo on hotline intake #2611 - Internal Audit memo IA-26-31, 30 October (prior-report): Auditors matched 120 call-back claims (April–August) against electronic gate-controller and restroom smart-lock event logs, including all 64 claims by Employees R-14 and R-22. For 117 of 120 claims (and 64 of 64 for R-14 and R-22), the logs show lock events at the claimed sites within 40 minutes of the claimed time. The three exceptions were at sites without smart locks, and supervisor sign-off sheets confirm attendance. Conclusion: no evidence of claims for work not performed. Observation: under the 3-hour minimum, each 30–45 minute closing round is paid as three hours.
331	C10 [stage S1] Recreation division event permit summary, April–September - Recreation permit system (system-record): Athletic field and pavilion permits issued: 1,284 (prior year 1,236, +4%). Events requiring staff attendance after 18:00: 61 (prior 58). Tournament weekends: 14 (prior 13). Event staffing overtime is charged to the Recreation cost center under pay code EV, not to the maintenance division.
332	C11 [stage S1] Fleet maintenance log for parks mowers and utility vehicles, January–September - City Fleet Services (log): Both mowers whose replacement was deferred remained in service. Unplanned mower downtime: 47 unit-days (prior year 39). Longest outage: 9 days (Riverside, June). On 6 occasions, work orders note that crews 'doubled up on remaining units.' No vehicle downtime affecting evening or night operations was recorded.
333	C12 [stage S1] Regional parks benchmarking survey: overtime share of maintenance payroll, prior fiscal year - Regional municipal parks association (external-data): Eight comparable municipalities. Overtime as a share of maintenance payroll: median 7.2%, range 4.1%–11.8%. Larkmoor, prior year: 6.9%. Figures are self-reported and the survey does not break out pay codes. Current-year figures have not yet been collected.
334	CANDIDATES
335	H1: The overtime increase is driven mainly by maintenance vacancies under the hiring freeze, with crews working extra hours to cover open routes.

You are adjudicating disagreements between a benchmark case's answer key and an independent expert's blind solution. For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.

Answer semantics:
- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to a substantive (not merely evidence-gathering) intervention? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

Truth convention: expected answers are what a careful analyst concludes after reading the initial file plus the optimal read path (at most three catalogue items); for INCOMPLETE and NOCONC cases, what the whole catalogue supports.

CASE OD2-DEV-OBVWRONG (OBVWRONG, organizational): Larkmoor Parks: the maintenance overtime overrun
Setting: The Larkmoor Parks and Open Space Department (fictional) maintains parks in four districts: Riverside, Eastgate, Millbrook and Summit Hill. The maintenance division has 112 maintenance-worker positions. This year the city adopted several budget reductions, including a citywide hiring freeze from 6 January. Maintenance overtime for April–September is well over budget, and the council's Finance Committee wants an explanation and a corrective plan.
Presenting request: The Budget Office has asked you to explain the overtime overrun in the parks maintenance division and recommend what the department should do before the Finance Committee deadline of 15 December. The Director believes the hiring freeze is the cause and has asked for an exemption to fill eleven positions.
INITIAL EVIDENCE
E1 [stage S1] Office of Budget & Management memo to the Parks Director (financial-record): Re: Overtime variance, April–September. Parks maintenance overtime for April–September totals $688,400, compared with $412,100 for the same months last year (+67%) and a budget of $430,000. Council's Finance Committee has asked for an explanation and corrective plan by 15 December. For reference, this year's adopted reductions for the department were: citywide hiring freeze on non-public-safety positions (from 6 January); deferral of two mower replacements ($118,000); non-renewal of the after-hours closing services contract ($96,000); reduced seasonal temp hours ($40,000). Please route your response through this office.
E2 [stage S1] Interview notes, Director Ruth Okafor-Lind, 3 November (leadership-account): 'This is the hiring freeze, plain and simple. We started the year six maintenance workers short and we're at seventeen now. Every vacancy is a route somebody has to cover after their shift. July was brutal too, because the heat meant extra irrigation checks and mowing catch-up. I've asked the City Manager for an exemption to fill eleven positions; that brings overtime back to normal within a quarter.' Asked about other drivers, she said the closing contract 'was a small line, crews absorbed it.' She said she had not seen a breakdown of overtime by pay code.
E3 [stage S1] HR/payroll extract prepared at the Director's request (system-record): Maintenance division, current year. Month: vacant maintenance-worker positions (of 112) / overtime paid. HR analyst note: correlation between monthly vacancies and monthly overtime, January–September, r = 0.93. 'Overtime has tracked the vacancy count closely all year.'
E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Dale Visconti, crew lead, Millbrook district, 5 November (staff-account): 'We're running routes two and three people short. Guys are holding over an hour or two most days to finish mowing. On top of that, since spring we're back out at night a few times a week, and nobody's seen their kids in months. Morale is the lowest I've seen in nineteen years. If they'd just fill the positions this would sort itself out.' He estimated he personally had worked 'about 25 hours of overtime a month' since April.
E5 [stage S1] City Ethics Hotline intake record #2611 (log): Received 22 August from an anonymous caller identifying as a parks employee. Allegation: two Riverside maintenance workers (named in the sealed record as Employees R-14 and R-22) 'are claiming night call-backs for parks they never go to. It's all paper slips, nobody checks. They're each pulling an extra grand a month.' Caller declined follow-up contact. Status: referred to Internal Audit for review on 26 August.
E6 [stage S1] Email from the Municipal Employees Local 418 steward to the Director, 7 November (staff-account): Members are exhausted and grievances are coming. Two points. Nobody wants a repeat of the splash-pad break-in two years ago. Fill the vacancies and treat people fairly.
E7 [stage S1] Risk Management quarterly summary, parks maintenance (system-record): Workers' compensation claims filed April–September: 15 (prior year, same period: 9). The directive does not restrict overtime or contract spending.
C2 [stage S1] Regional weather station summary, April–September, current and prior year - Larkmoor airport weather station (external-data): Days at or above 35°C: 6 (prior year 2). By pay code: OT-X holdover $341.0k → $358.1k (hours +1.5%; rest reflects the 3.5% July wage increase); CB call-back $38.2k → $289.3k; other (holiday, storm, event) $32.9k → $41.0k. Each entry lists date, time of injury, task and injury type; the district field is blank on most entries. 11 of 15 injuries occurred between 07:00 and 13:00; 9 involved mowing, trimming or lifting. C8 [stage S1] Interview with the Eastgate district supervisor - Interview notes, Marisol Adeyemi-Clark, Eastgate supervisor, 10 November (manager-account): 'I post a sign-up sheet every Monday for the week's closings. C9 [stage S1] Internal Audit memo on hotline intake #2611 - Internal Audit memo IA-26-31, 30 October (prior-report): Auditors matched 120 call-back claims (April–August) against electronic gate-controller and restroom smart-lock event logs, including all 64 claims by Employees R-14 and R-22. The three exceptions were at sites without smart locks, and supervisor sign-off sheets confirm attendance. Conclusion: no evidence of claims for work not performed. C10 [stage S1] Recreation division event permit summary, April–September - Recreation permit system (system-record): Athletic field and pavilion permits issued: 1,284 (prior year 1,236, +4%). Events requiring staff attendance after 18:00: 61 (prior 58). Tournament weekends: 14 (prior 13). Event staffing overtime is charged to the Recreation cost center under pay code EV, not to the maintenance division.

No vehicle downtime affecting evening or night operations was recorded.
